benefits: Answers 'how much flooring do I need' in one screen.
Converts area to whole boxes with the coverage you enter.
Adjustable waste for straight lays, diagonals, and odd rooms.

faqs.a: Multiply length x width. A 12 x 15 ft room is 180 sq ft. Then add waste: 10% for straight lays, 15% for diagonal or irregular rooms.
faqs.q: How do I calculate how much flooring I need?

faqs.a: 10% is standard for straight plank layouts. Use 15% for diagonal patterns, rooms with many corners, or wide planks with more cuts.
faqs.q: What waste percentage should I use?

faqs.a: Divide your needed square feet by the box coverage and round up. 198 sq ft / 20 sq ft per box = 9.9, so buy 10 boxes.
faqs.q: How many boxes of flooring do I need?

faqs.a: Keep at least one full box. Future repairs need the same dye lot, and manufacturers discontinue colors regularly.

faqs.q: Do I measure in square feet or square meters?
faqs.a: Either — this tool accepts feet or meters and shows both square feet and square meters. Suppliers usually sell by the box with coverage printed in square feet, so the box count uses your entered coverage.

faqs.q: How do I measure an L-shaped room?
faqs.a: Split it into two rectangles, measure each, and add the areas. For example, a 10 x 12 ft main area plus a 6 x 4 ft alcove = 120 + 24 = 144 sq ft before waste.

flooring-calculator.formula:
area (sq ft) = length x width
needed = area x (1 + waste%)
boxes = ceil(needed / box coverage in sq ft)
extra = boxes x coverage - needed

flooring-calculator.workedExample:
A 12 x 15 ft living room, 10% waste, boxes covering 20 sq ft:

1. Area = 12 x 15 = 180 sq ft.
2. Needed = 180 x 1.10 = 198 sq ft (18.39 sq m).
3. Boxes = ceil(198 / 20) = ceil(9.9) = 10 boxes.
4. Extra = 10 x 20 - 198 = 2 sq ft left over.

Buy 10 boxes and keep the leftover pieces for future repairs.
